claim: After a successful device-bound remote relay mutation, the administering installation can publish a capability-free, project/room/action/result-bound signed statement into bounded shared project state. Independent verification, offline reopen, disconnected convergence, and contradictory-revision retention pass; the statement is not signed by the relay and grants no authority.
proved: The native signer uses a separate syzygy-project-relay-admin-decision-v1 domain and binds project, room, administrator member, exact expected/resulting revisions, affected member, semantic action SHA-256, record time, and a random 32-byte nonce.
Strict frontend parsing requires exact fields, canonical base64url, exact key/signature sizes, recomputed key identity, capability-free action shapes, and a non-status mutation.
The builder accepts only a relay result for the same project, room, next revision, affected member, credential generation, role, and revocation state; mismatched native signer output is rejected.
Publication requires an independently verified, unconflicted project-directory entry for the signer, derives storage identity from all revision/key/nonce fields, and is idempotent.
Distinct disconnected decisions converge and reopen offline; concurrent contradictory statements for one resulting revision remain visible and make history read-only.

The exact project-bound relay protocol still passes five-client rapid-write, partition/rejoin, awareness recovery, viewer filtering, fresh reauthentication, replay denial, and remote issue/rotate/revoke gates.

Product copy distinguishes an installation statement from relay authority, surfaces post-success recording failure without rolling back the relay action, and never stores the returned capability in shared history.
notProved: The relay signed, acknowledged, or independently attested to a decision record.
A registered installation key belongs to a verified person or organization or that the project directory grants its relay role.
The ledger is complete, append-only, server-ordered, deletion-resistant, or protected from a Yjs writer who withholds, replays, deletes, or floods records.
Host-local relay administration is represented in this remote-device decision path.
General policy, scenario, review, or other durable research events are signed.
Administrator-key recovery, trusted time, packaged physical two-install interaction, or third-party relay behavior.
